    r['shift']=r.post-r.pre; r['z']=r['shift']/(r.prestd+1)
    print(c);print(r.sort_values('shift',ascending=False).head(12).round(1).to_string())
    new=p.columns[(p.loc[:D-pd.Timedelta(days=1)].sum()==0)&(p.loc[D]>0)];print('new',list(new))"}

**How I found it:** I took the account's cost on 2025-06-30 and compared it with the average for 16–29 June. I did this for each breakdown in the data: cloud service, application and instance family. The account total rose from about 59,600–60,500 per day on 27–29 June to about 73,800 on 30 June. It then stayed around 68,000–69,000 on 1 and 2 July.

- **grK stepped up and stayed up.** For the 18 days before the anomaly it cost a flat 825–835 per day. It then jumped to about 3,680 on 30 June, 3,661 on 1 July and 3,680 on 2 July. At about +2,850 versus baseline, this was the largest increase of any application.
- **All of grK's six instance families moved together.** Each one rose about 4.4 to 4.5 times on 30 June and held that level.     print('new:',list(p.index[(p.loc[:,p.columns<A].sum(1)==0)]))"}

- **4GC6s2S4LL** (application QTP, cloud service ptWbQ): cost went from a flat ~$91/day in the two weeks before to ~$3,062/day from 2025-08-22 on. That's about +$2,971/day. It accounts for the whole jump in QTP (~$821 to ~$3,814/day) and in service ptWbQ (~$2.8k to ~$5.9k/day, still high through 08-26). QTP's other five families didn't change.
- **MDpKclV0vO** (application Yp5, cloud service XsWXE): cost went from a flat ~$9.7/day to ~$2,981/day from 2025-08-22 on, also about +$2,971/day. It accounts for the whole Yp5 increase (~$187 to ~$3,155/day). Yp5's other families stayed flat.

Because only one family moved in each application, I'm reporting the families rather than the applications.

I left out three things on purpose:
- **kZ4sKQTQYv** (application EsT, service G6pNo) spiked to ~$2,458 on 08-22 only, which also explains G6pNo's one-day spike to ~$4.6k. G6pNo was back at ~$2.2k/day the next day, so this was a one-day burst, not a new level.
- **L03Wp**, the largest service, swings a lot from day to day anyway (about $5.8k to $20k), so it isn't a new level.
- No other family or application moved by more than about $200/day.

The root cause is the application **amm**. Its daily cost rose from about $630–710 to about $2,080–2,230 on 2025-12-18 and stayed there through 12-21, the last day in the data.

1. **The total spike was mostly temporary.** The account's cost was about $51K–56.5K a day from 12-04 to 12-17. It jumped to $60,335 on 12-18 and fell back to about $52K–55K over 12-19 to 12-21. Most of the extra cost on the anomaly date did not last, but one part did.

2. **amm is the only lasting step up that starts on 12-18.**
   - I compared each of the 12-18 to 12-21 days with 12-04 to 12-17. Only six instance families stayed above their highest baseline value on all four days, and all six belong to amm: Lx5RJ349Vr, hKa71k39sH, KSd3btDldV, J866NQtQrD, B2oo8JKZ7k and eb3oYXxaPD.
   - Those six are all of amm's instance families, and they all stepped up on the same day to about 3–4 times their earlier level. For example, hKa71k39sH went from $180 to $581 a day, and Lx5RJ349Vr went from about $360 to about $1,110 on average.
   - Because the whole application moved together, I'm reporting amm rather than its individual instance families. It was the largest increase by application on 12-18, at about +$1,400 against the two-week average.

3. **The other big increases on 12-18 were short bursts, so I left them out.**

for c in ['application','instance_family']:
    p=d.pivot_table(index='date',columns=c,values='unblended_cost',aggfunc='sum').fillna(0)
    pre=p.loc[t-pd.Timedelta(days=14):t-pd.Timedelta(days=1)];post=p.loc[t:]
    first=(p>0).idxmax()
    s=pd.DataFrame({'pre':pre.mean(),'sd':pre.std(),'post':post.mean(),'postmin':post.min(),'first':first})
    s['z']=(s.post-s.pre)/s.sd.replace(0,1)
    s['minz']=(s.postmin-pre.max())
    print(s.sort_values('z').tail(8).round(1))
    print('new on/after:',s[s['first']>=t-pd.Timedelta(days=3)])"}
